name: Dysmorphism-Cleft Palate-Loose Skin Syndrome
aliases: Dysmorphism with Cleft Palate and Cutis Laxa Syndrome
Dysmorphic Cleft Palate Loose Skin Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Dysmorphism-Cleft Palate-Loose Skin Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of cleft palate (either isolated or with cleft lip)
Generalized loose, redundant, and wrinkled skin resembling cutis laxa
Characteristic facial dysmorphic features including hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and micrognathia
Presence of joint hypermobility and hypotonia
Postnatal growth retardation or failure to thrive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: cleft palate, loose skin, and characteristic facial dysmorphism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing may support but is not definitive.

laboratory: Possible mild anemia secondary to feeding difficulties
imaging: Craniofacial CT or MRI showing cleft palate and facial bone abnormalities
Echocardiography to assess for cardiac defects
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal recessive inheritance
Genetic testing may exclude other syndromes with overlapping features
other: Skin biopsy may show elastin abnormalities consistent with cutis laxa

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent systemic involvement including pulmonary emphysema
Known genetic mutations in elastin or fibulin genes
Hypertelorism with bifid uvula rather than cleft palate

redFlags: Severe feeding difficulties leading to failure to thrive
Respiratory distress due to cleft palate complications
Signs of cardiac defects or heart failure
references: Recent case reports and clinical reviews in medical genetics literature
